questions.question: You open an existing file with mode "w". What happens to its old contents?
options: They're kept, new text is added at the end
questions.explanation: "w" (write) empties the file first. Use "a" (append) to add to the end instead.

questions.question: Why use `with open(...) as f:`?
options: It closes the file automatically, even if an error happens
questions.explanation: Files must be closed or data may not be saved. 'with' closes the file when the block ends, whatever happens.

questions.question: What does `Path(__file__).parent / "data.txt"` give you?
options: data.txt in the terminal's current folder
data.txt in the same folder as the running script
questions.explanation: __file__ is the script's own path, so .parent is its folder. This works no matter where you run the script from.

questions.question: Which function saves a Python dict to a JSON file?
questions.explanation: json.dump writes data to a file; json.load reads it back. f.write(data) would fail, because write() needs a string.
